messages:
maya_ml: Heads-up — we've observed a sustained drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate for gptx-large on the /chat/stream route over the last 6h. Token-saved metric down ~28% vs baseline. Graph on the dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/rt-cache/prefix-hitrate?panel=7 :frowning:
alex_dev: Ugh. Any recent changes to batching or kernel selection that could explain it?
maya_ml: We rolled batching heuristic v2 at 02:00 UTC (more aggressive aggregation for sub-8-token requests) and a kernel patch to force fp16 conv kernels on this model at 02:10. Both coincide with the drop window.
tony_sre: infra-bot shows the deploys:
infra-bot: deploy/serving-heuristics v2 -> prod at 2026-03-01T02:00Z
infra-bot: kernel/fp16-conv -> prod at 2026-03-01T02:10Z
rachael_pm: Customer SRE reported increased 95p latency for small chat shards, maybe related. They flagged production incidents around 02:30.
sam_research: I pulled profiler traces — KV lookup tail latency is fine, but hit-rate per-key is dropping. Investigated key churn: many keys include ephemeral session metadata. Current keying: `customer_id|route|prompt_hash|session_ts_truncated` — the `session_ts_truncated` is 1-minute resolution which might be causing lower reuse for quick follow-ups.
maya_ml: Here's the PromQL I'm using for per-route hit-rate (raw):

```
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{route="\/chat\/stream",model="gptx-large"}[5m]))
/
sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{route="\/chat\/stream",model="gptx-large"}[5m]))
```

sam_research: And aggregated per-customer token-saved:

```
sum by(customer_id) (rate(kv_cache_tokens_saved_total[5m]))
```

maya_ml: Initial hypothesis: the batching heuristic v2 increases request queuing and changes micro-batching boundaries, which causes slightly different prompt concatenations and therefore different prompt_hash values when we compute keys server-side. Combined with the conv kernel change (which modified tokenization warm path for fp16 padding), warmup behavior got worse.
alex_dev: So keying + batching = regression in logical cache hit rate, not necessarily underlying KV perf.
maya_ml: Exactly. Two mitigations I want to try:
- short-term: strip `session_ts_truncated` and replace with `session_bucket=5s` (reduce churn) for chat routes to improve reuse for quick follow-ups
- medium-term: add a deterministic canonicalization step for prompt hashing (normalize whitespace, remove ephemeral system tokens)
- alternative: keep keying as-is but add a warmup prefetch when a new session is detected (fetch likely next prefixes from model rollout traces)

tony_sre: Sounds sensible. Any risk to token accounting / privacy with canonicalization? We must avoid normalizing customer PII into same key across users.
maya_ml: We'll keep `customer_id` in key and canonicalization will be applied only to system assistant/template parts; user messages remain unchanged. Will run a check to ensure no cross-customer collisions.
rachael_pm: What's the expected impact on token-saved if we fix this?
sam_research: Based on sampling, if we reduce key churn we can recover ~60% of the lost hit-rate -> ~17% token-saved improvement back. I posted a short notebook with sample estimates: https://notebooks.redwood.com/u/sam/prefix-reuse-sim
alex_dev: Can we surface per-customer regressions on the hit-rate dashboard so CS can triage affected tenants? Current panels are per-model and per-route only.
maya_ml: I put up a draft panel: per-customer rolling hit-rate + tokens-saved, and sticky flag for 'recent deploys' so you can overlay deploy timeline. Link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/rt-cache/prefix-hitrate-per-customer
infra-bot: alert: create_alert if per-customer hit-rate drops > 20% for > 15m
tony_sre: We'll enable that alert in prod for the next 48h while we test mitigations.
maya_ml: Plan for next 24h:
1) revert batching heuristic v2 in a canary region (tony)
2) deploy keying change (strip session_ts_truncated -> session_bucket 5s) behind feature flag (alex)
3) run A/B on kernel patch rollback vs fp16 padding fallback (sam + infra)
4) observe dashboards: model-route-customer hit-rate, token-saved, per-request caching decisions log (trace ids)

alex_dev: For observability, can we add a sampled event log for cache misses that records: prompt_hash, batch_id, kernel_variant, and hint (keyed_by) ? Short list of fields only, sampled 0.1%.
maya_ml: Yes — I added a PR for sampled cache-miss telemetry. It includes `prompt_hash`, `route`, `model_variant`, `batch_boundary_id`, `kern_variant` and `customer_id` (hashed). No raw prompt text.
rachael_pm: Customer comms: I'll draft a note for any affected mid-market customers explaining we saw transient cache regressions after a runtime tweak and that we're rolling mitigations.
managers: :eyes: (react)

sam_research: Quick note — profiling trace shows that when miss rate spikes, KV eviction churn increases and LRU scans create more CPU pressure on the serving host. That may explain the small latency bump customers saw.
maya_ml: Good catch. We'll add eviction stats to the dashboard: evictions/sec and avg-eviction-scan-time.
alex_dev: Anything else we need before rolling changes?
maya_ml: Need approvals for the canary rollback from infra and signoff on telemetry PR. If both green, we'll roll fixes and re-evaluate within 2 hours.

alex_dev: I'll schedule the rollback canary and add a runbook note under /runbooks/prefix-cache-regression.md
maya_ml: Thanks. I'll post updates in this thread as we see numbers. :thumbsup:
